studies.label: Classroom experiment: GenAI-supported, peer-collaborative, and individual creative writing

counts_source.locator: PDF p. 1, Abstract, Methods (total and arm counts); PDF p. 4, Section 3.1 (random assignment, no participation refusals); PDF p. 7, Table 1 (analysis N by arm)
counts_source.quote: An experiment involved 78 primary school students in China assigned to three conditions: GenAI-­supported writing (n = 20), peer collaboration (n = 38; 19 pairs), and individual writing (n = 20).

arms.name: GenAI-supported writing group
arms.description: Students used Deepseek on computers as a thinking partner while writing, following a task-specific tutorial and instructions to select, evaluate, and revise suggestions. Final essays were handwritten (PDF pp. 4-6, Sections 3.1-3.3).

arms.name: Peer-collaborative writing group
arms.description: Students worked with a peer in 19 pairs and produced handwritten writing. The paper does not explain whether partners shared one essay or how scores were assigned to partners (PDF p. 4, Section 3.1; PDF p. 5, Section 3.2).

arms.name: Individual writing group
arms.description: Students completed the writing task independently by hand, without the AI or peer assistance assigned to the other arms (PDF p. 4, Section 3.1; PDF p. 5, Section 3.2).

studies.task: Fifth-grade students wrote an essay, Design Future Cars, of around 300 words within 25 minutes during the intervention session (PDF p. 5, Section 3.3; PDF p. 6, Section 3.3).

ai_tool.name: Deepseek (model version not stated)
ai_tool.locator: PDF p. 5, Section 3.3: The GenAI tool used in this study was Deepseek. No model version or release year is specified.

estimates.question: with_ai
estimates.measure_detail: Three researchers independently rated each handwritten intervention essay on a 100-point creativity rubric: originality (40 points), flexibility (30 points), and elaboration (30 points). Only the total is reported. The scoring rule uses the raters' average when inter-rater reliability is high; the paper describes intervention-essay reliability as satisfactory. Discussion to consensus is described for the baseline essays. Rater blinding is not stated (PDF p. 6, Sections 3.3-3.4).

estimates.notes: Table 1 reports student-level N, means, and SDs; scores are not individual rater observations. The ANOVA test, its p-value, partial eta-squared, and Cohen's f concern all three arms and are not pairwise statistics, so test, p_value, and paper_effect are null here. The LSD column reports only letter orderings, with no numeric pairwise difference, SE, CI, or p-value. No contrast-specific total people count is printed, so n_total is null rather than a calculated sum. The LSD column gives a > c. Each student in these two arms produced an essay; se_basis and sd_level follow the reported participant-level analysis. The AI arm is shared with the AI-versus-peer contrast.

estimates.notes: Table 1 reports student-level N, means, and SDs; scores are not individual rater observations. The ANOVA test, its p-value, partial eta-squared, and Cohen's f concern all three arms and are not pairwise statistics, so test, p_value, and paper_effect are null here. The LSD column reports only letter orderings, with no numeric pairwise difference, SE, CI, or p-value. No contrast-specific total people count is printed, so n_total is null rather than a calculated sum. The LSD column gives a > b. The peer arm is called Peer-collaborative group in Table 1; the screening-form arm name is retained. unit, sd_level, and se_basis describe the reported student-level analysis, not verified independence: the paper counts 38 peer-arm students but describes 19 pairs (PDF p. 4, Section 3.1). It does not explain whether an essay score was shared by partners or report any adjustment for partner dependence. The peer contrast needs this dependence issue resolved before treating its precision as suitable for pooling. The AI arm is shared with the AI-versus-individual contrast.

not_extracted.what: Correlations of writing self-efficacy and flow state with creative writing performance
not_extracted.reason: Associations involving self-reports, not randomized AI-arm contrasts on output outcomes (Sections 4.2-4.3, PDF pp. 7-8).

not_extracted.what: Student-AI interaction patterns: prompt functions and AI-content uptake
not_extracted.reason: Descriptive coding within the AI arm only, with no comparison-arm contrast. Uptake concerns links between AI responses and a student's essay, not diversity across different people (PDF p. 6, Section 3.4; PDF p. 8, Section 4.4 and Table 4).

not_extracted.what: Creative writing performance: peer-collaborative versus individual writing
not_extracted.reason: Neither arm received generative AI, so this is not an eligible AI contrast (PDF p. 4, Section 3.1; PDF p. 7, Table 1, LSD b > c).

open_items: Peer-arm dependence is unresolved: the reported analysis counts 38 students although they worked in 19 pairs. The paper does not identify independent essays, shared scores, or partner-adjusted uncertainty. The participant codes describe the paper's analysis and do not establish that the peer-arm precision is valid for pooling (PDF p. 4, Section 3.1; PDF p. 7, Table 1).

Pairwise numerical test statistics, p-values, standard errors, confidence intervals, and standardized effects are not printed. Only the arm means/SDs/Ns and LSD letter orderings are available. Contrast-specific total people counts are not separately printed and were not calculated (PDF p. 7, Table 1).
Separate originality, flexibility, and elaboration results are unavailable; the paper reports only the total creative-writing rubric score (PDF p. 6, Section 3.4; PDF p. 7, Table 1).
The Deepseek model version and release year are not specified (PDF p. 5, Section 3.3).
Random assignment of participants is explicit, but sequence generation, allocation implementation, and handling of the source classes are not described (PDF p. 4, Section 3.1).
Blinding of the researcher raters to condition is not stated (PDF p. 6, Sections 3.3-3.4).
Arm-level baseline creativity means and SDs are not printed (PDF p. 4, Section 3.1).
notes: Reconciled independently against the complete markdown conversion, read consecutively through the end of the references, and the PDF. The supplied diff contains no study-field or estimate-field disagreements and no estimates present in only one extraction. No substantive extraction value required correction, and no additional eligible estimate was found; resolutions is therefore empty. A's slugs are retained; differences in descriptive wording and whitespace do not identify different estimates. Both Table 1 contrasts for S1-O1 are included. S1-O2 and S1-O3, baseline writing, the unreported rubric subscores, correlations, the AI-arm process analysis, and the comparison between the two non-AI arms are listed in not_extracted. No across-people diversity or outcome after AI removal is reported. PDF text was extracted for every cited page; PDF pp. 5 and 7 were also rendered in memory to check Figure 1 and results prose missing from the text layer. PDF page numbers match printed page numbers. No appendix or separate supplement is referenced in the document. Agreement audit: PDF p. 4, Section 3.1 explicitly randomizes participants, and PDF p. 1, Abstract reports the total and all arm counts. Table 1 (PDF p. 7) repeats the assigned counts as analysis N; no attrition or participant exclusions are reported. The counts are people, including all peer-arm students, rather than pairs, essays, or raters. No pairwise combined total is printed, so n_total stays null. The classroom context supports field_rct; the source classes and peer pairs are not reported as randomization clusters (PDF pp. 4-5, Sections 3.1-3.2). Figure 1 and Section 3.2 establish one common pre-intervention baseline followed by a between-person writing intervention, not a randomized-order crossover; within_person is null for both contrasts. AI was available during production of the scored intervention essay, so question is with_ai, outcome_with_ai is true, and timing is immediate (PDF p. 5, Section 3.2 and Figure 1). The total combines originality, flexibility, and elaboration, supporting overall_creativity and higher_is=more_creative; it is not a general writing-proficiency score despite the informational task genre (PDF p. 6, Sections 3.3-3.4; PDF p. 10, Section 6). The researchers scored essays and combined rater scores, while Table 1 indexes the analysis by students, supporting expert_raters, unit=participant, and sd_level=participant. For the peer contrast, these codes and se_basis=participant describe the reported nominal analysis; they do not establish independent scores or partner-adjusted precision. The unresolved pairing issue is retained in open_items and the estimate notes. All extracted means, SDs, and arm counts were checked in the PDF table. Decimal precision is preserved in the JSON numeric literals and source quotes; quotes normalize whitespace only. The omnibus ANOVA and effect sizes describe the complete three-arm comparison and are not attached to either pairwise estimate. The LSD column reports orderings only, so numeric pairwise tests, p-values, differences, standard errors, and confidence intervals remain null. No preregistration or designated primary outcome is stated (PDF p. 2, research questions; complete document reviewed), and no shared sample is identified in the screening form or paper. Data are available from the corresponding author upon reasonable request; no public data URL is given (PDF p. 11, Data Availability Statement). The missing baseline summaries, rubric subscores, randomization details, rater blinding, pairwise precision, and peer-score dependence in the screening form remain open. No effect statistic, combined count, or missing model release year was derived or guessed.
